Case A: A pharmacist licensed in another state obtains NABP approval of a Massachusetts reciprocity application and assumes that a Massachusetts license is now active.

Case B: A pharmacist has held licenses in several states and is assembling a Massachusetts reciprocity application. One license has a disciplinary history.

Which proposed interpretation is INCORRECT? Select ONE answer.

A.original_option_text: A personal appearance is replaced by an employer reference in every reciprocity case.

B.original_option_text: Massachusetts MPJE requirements remain part of the applicable reciprocity pathway.

C.original_option_text: The application must address the required standing of all states in which licenses were held.

D.original_option_text: NABP's preliminary approval does not replace the Massachusetts Board's final decision.

Case B: A pharmacist wants to restart the reciprocity application period by changing employers after NABP approval.

C.original_option_text: Timely NABP approval removes the remaining state licensing requirements.

D.original_option_text: Every one-year licensing deadline uses the date of the most recent examination.

Case A: A pharmacist manages both a personal Massachusetts pharmacist registration and a Drug Store Pharmacy license and tries to renew both on the same two-year schedule.

D.original_option_text: Renewing the personal pharmacist license also renews the facility licenses.

Case A: A Massachusetts pharmacist allowed a non-disciplinary license to expire 75 days ago. The pharmacist wants to resume practice after merely mailing the renewal fee.

Case B: Another pharmacist's non-disciplinary registration has been unrenewed for more than two years. The pharmacist asks whether the same short-lapse process necessarily applies.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

A.original_option_text: An ordinary lapse longer than two years can be resolved by paying fees alone.

B.original_option_text: An expired registration must be treated as a disciplinary revocation in every case.

C.original_option_text: Proof of a mailed renewal payment permits practice under an expired registration.

D.original_option_text: A lapse exceeding 60 days can trigger Board-specified conditions, including additional CE.

Case A: A pharmacist without an exemption completes 40 accepted CE hours in one calendar year and none in the next, then attests to meeting the Massachusetts renewal requirements.

Case B: A pharmacist completes more than the minimum this year and wants to assign the excess hours to next year's annual requirement.

Which conclusion correctly addresses Case A? Select ONE answer.

A.original_option_text: The annual minimum must be met in each calendar year, not merely in the biennial total.

B.original_option_text: One live law hour counts as two hours toward the overall annual total.

C.original_option_text: Excess annual hours automatically become next year's first CE credits.

D.original_option_text: The ordinary annual completion deadline is the date the employer reviews the file.

Case A: A pharmacist graduated from an ACPE-accredited school several years ago and transfers a license to Massachusetts on October 12. The pharmacist assumes the entire new-license year is CE-exempt.
